# Annabelle (01, engineer) — SPD-080

## Brief
Write a project skill that teaches the rules bin/spudlib/ was built on, and a reporting-only probe that lists application code past the size thresholds. Full context is the ticket brief: run `spud --as <your id> member show SPUD-080/<your name>`.

The one-sentence version: after SPD-065 split bin/spud_ledger.py (10663 lines) into a 191-line orchestrator over 58 modules, Eric wants new and changed code to keep that shape rather than drift back. The skill is the teaching; the probe is the nudge; neither may become a gate.

Eric's size rule, exactly: ~250 lines is the point at which a module is worth a second look, never a cap. A module may be as large as it needs to be, and the larger it gets the more it must justify itself. No cohesive function, class or region is ever cut to fit a number. Application code only; tests, stylesheets and HTML are out of scope. The current package honours this: largest module bin/spudlib/projects/install.py at 348 lines, eleven modules over 250, each deliberate.

The skill has to carry the constraints that actually bite here, each with its reason, not as a list of rules to obey:
- Real modules importing whole modules (Eric's decision over a one-namespace design), and why importing a name by value breaks the suite's monkeypatching at the call site.
- The hook path's import set: every Bash, Edit and Agent call runs the PreToolUse hook, so a hook imports only its own event's modules; render, import, the parser, project install, schedule and doctor stay off it. How a new module stays off it, and how a hook change is timed with tests/probes/hook_timing.py (within 1 ms of main).
- The loader and interpreter: python3.14 -I -S, nothing on sys.path, the finder that answers only spudlib from beside the entry, bytecode cached under the home's state directory, the entry refusing to run directly.
- Where a new module goes among the nine directories, and what belongs in each.
- The one guarded import cycle in the shell analysis, and that a second is a smell, not a precedent.
- What tests/test_package.py already guards, pointed at rather than repeated.

Read first: docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md (the approved design), docs/spikes/spd-065/review.md, bin/spud, bin/spud_ledger.py, the bin/spudlib/ tree, tests/test_package.py, tests/probes/hook_timing.py, CLAUDE.md, and ledger/tickets/SPD-065.md.

Deliverables, and only these:
- .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md — a Claude Code project skill: `name` and `description` frontmatter, the description written so it triggers when a session is about to write or change code under bin/. One skill, unless you find two genuinely distinct trigger moments; if you write two, say why in your result. Write for a reader who has never seen this package.
- tests/probes/module_sizes.py — shaped like tests/probes/hook_timing.py: run by hand, prints what it found, exits 0 whatever it finds. Application code only, never tests. It names both bands, the ~250 look-again point and the 1000-line refactor trigger that started SPD-065 and BAD-036, as report bands and not as pass or fail. Its header says plainly that it is advisory.
- tests/test_module_sizes.py — only if the probe has behaviour worth pinning (file selection and banding, most likely). Match the suite's idiom.

CLAUDE.md is Spud's and is NOT yours to edit: name in your result the exact lines you would add (the size rule for the rules section, and the probe's invocation for Commands) and Spud writes them.

Done when: the skill would guide a stranger correctly, the probe runs clean on this tree and prints an honest report, `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes in full, and no bytecode is left under bin/ or tests/. Quote the suite's tail in your result.

Application code only: no file under a directory named tests is ever read whatever path it is given, nor a test_*.py; bin/spud is included by its shebang. Default root is bin/; a path argument can point it at another project's tree.
